method: every requirement line and every §8 row compared by hand with the boards' pictures and captions; SHOWN = the design draws it as the PRD says; DIFFERENT = register row; NOT SHOWN = no picture (register BT-N rows); NO SCREEN = PRD says no screen change

rows.prd_words: When a default other than the customer itself is saved, the customer page left card shows "Bill Invoices To" with the payer's name.
Users who may set the default see "Change" beside the name; it opens the "Bill Invoices To" window.
The window shows the help line "New work orders and part sales for [customer] will be billed to this customer. Existing ones don't change."
The window has a searchable "Bill Invoices To" field and a "Save" button.
The field's first option is "[customer] (this customer)"; picking it and saving clears the default.
rows.note: clearing by '(this customer)' is caption only

rows.prd_words: Saving applies only to work orders and part sales created afterwards.
When at least one customer has this customer as its default, the card shows a "Pays for" counter beside Contacts and Assets, with the count.
The counter's tooltip reads "Customers billed to this customer by default".
Clicking the counter opens a window titled "[customer] pays for", listing each customer A to Z as a link to its page; a long list scrolls inside the window.
rows.note: one customer only; long list scroll BT-N01

rows.prd_words: The window shows the line "These customers bill new work orders and part sales to [customer] by default." and a "Close" button.
A customer that bills itself shows no "Bill Invoices To" line and no way to set one on the card; the default is set in New Customer or Edit Customer (Story 2).
Without 'Customers → Create & Edit' or 'View and Manage AP/AR Data', "Change" is hidden; the line still shows.
On Counter Sale, "Change" is hidden.
rows.note: Counter Sale card with a saved default is impossible (S1 Error Handling); no picture

rows.prd_words: The "Pays for" counter is hidden when the count is 0.
Counter Sale never appears in the field's options.
rows.where: bt-p3-18 (work order field); customer windows not searched for Counter Sale

rows.prd_words: One hop only: if the payer has its own default, new work orders still bill the payer, not the payer's default.
New Customer and Edit Customer show a searchable "Bill Invoices To" field, reading "This customer" until another customer is picked.
The field sits after Credit Terms | Credit Limit and before Sales Representative (context: field order shared with SV-11638 and SV-10890).
Edit Customer shows the help line "New work orders and part sales bill to this customer. Existing ones don't change." under the field.
In New Customer, the first option reads "[name typed so far] (this customer)", or "New customer (this customer)" before a name is typed.
rows.note: typed name only; 'New customer (this customer)' BT-N03

rows.prd_words: The pick saves together with the window's Save; if any part fails, nothing is saved and no customer is created.
An empty Address 2 is hidden; a + button beside Address 1 (tooltip "Add Address 2") shows it.
A shown Address 2 has an x button (tooltip "Remove Address 2") that clears and hides it; nothing is saved until Save.
A customer whose Address 2 holds a value opens with Address 2 showing, even when Address 1 is empty.
rows.note: Address 1 not empty in the picture

rows.prd_words: Without 'View and Manage AP/AR Data', the field is hidden and the window closes up around it.
New Customer shows no help line under the field.
On Counter Sale, Edit Customer shows no "Bill Invoices To" field.
The card's expanded section shows a "Bill To" field under Authorizer.
The field reads "This customer" when the customer pays for itself, otherwise the Bill To's name.
Typing searches every customer in the organization except Counter Sale, A to Z, showing the first 50 matches; the first option is always "[customer] (this customer)".
rows.where: bt-p2-03 (A to Z), bt-p3-17/21 (current Bill To second)

rows.prd_words: With no match, the list shows only the "(this customer)" option.
Picking a customer saves the Bill To immediately; picking "(this customer)" makes the customer pay for itself.
A new work order or part sale starts billed to the customer's saved default, if any, else the customer itself.
Splitting a work order or part sale, or reopening a paid work order onto a new one, copies its Bill To to the new one.
New Work Order and New Part Sale show no Bill To.
On a Counter Sale work order or part sale, any customer except Counter Sale can be picked as Bill To.
Users without the permission see the field only when someone else pays, read-only.
In history mode the field is read-only, shown only when someone else pays, with no lock message.
Invoiced or holding deposits: see Story 5.
The Authorizer list shows "No authorizer", then the customer's authorizer contacts, then the Bill To's.
Each contact shows its customer's name on a second line.
A contact of the current Bill To can be saved as Authorizer and prints as the authorizer on documents.
Changing the Bill To clears an Authorizer who is a contact of the previous Bill To, with no message.
Change Customer clears the Authorizer, as today, including a contact of a Bill To that stays.
When the customer pays for itself, the list is exactly today's, with no second line.
An Authorizer from the customer stays when the Bill To changes.
A contact of any other customer is refused, as today.
When Invoiced, the Bill To field is read-only with M4 as its tooltip.
Clicking or tapping the Invoiced field shows M4 as an error toast with a "Go To Invoice" button.
"Go To Invoice" opens the work order's or part sale's Finance tab; it never reverses anything.
While deposits are held on an Open document, the field is read-only with M1 as its tooltip.
Clicking or tapping that field shows M1 as an error toast with an "Open Deposits" button.
"Open Deposits" opens the Deposits tab of the customer holding the largest share of the deposits.
M1 names the total not reversed and the customer it was taken from, or "[N] customers" when there are several.
rows.note: one deposit, one customer; other forms BT-N08

rows.prd_words: After the invoice is reversed, or all deposits are reversed, the field unlocks.
Without 'Invoicing & payments → View' and 'See Financial Data', the M4 toast shows with no button.
Without 'View and Manage AP/AR Data' and 'Customers → View', the M1 toast shows with no button.
Users who cannot change the Bill To get M1 or M4 as an error toast on click or tap, with no button.
If the document is invoiced while the page is open, a change is refused with M4 and the field refreshes to its locked state.
If a deposit is taken while the page is open, a change is refused with M1 and its button, and the field refreshes.
When the document is both Invoiced and holds deposits, M4 shows.
If the Bill To was the old customer or the old customer's saved default, it follows to the new customer's saved default, else the new customer.
A Bill To picked on purpose stays after Change Customer.
The existing deposit block on Change Customer applies only when the change would change the Bill To.
On an Invoiced document, the invoice keeps its Bill To. A self-billed document stays self-billed, so invoicing again after Reverse bills the new customer, as today.
If the picked Bill To is the new customer, the document becomes self-billed.
The invoice's Bill To block prints the Bill To's name, address and phone, saved on the invoice when it is created.
rows.note: BT-D05 legacy prints no phone; modern prints it

rows.prd_words: The Bill To's credit term, saved on the invoice, sets the due date.
rows.note: due date not demonstrable from the pictures

rows.prd_words: Pricing, tax, discounts, fees and shop supplies are the customer's; changing the Bill To never changes the total.
The Bill To's "PO is required" applies to Customer PO.
The Over Credit warning measures the Bill To's limit against everything the Bill To owes; it never blocks.
If the Bill To is on Credit Hold, the Credit Hold banner reads M2 with a "Change Bill To" button (work orders: page header; part sales: Finance tab).
"Change Bill To" opens and focuses the Customer card's Bill To field; on a phone it first opens the work order details.
The Create Invoice action is disabled with M2 as its tooltip.
If Create Invoice is reached anyway or the server refuses it, M2 shows as an error toast with a "Change Bill To" button, and no invoice is created.
The server refuses an invoice for a Bill To on Credit Hold with M2, however the Credit Hold term is capitalized.
The work order's Credit Hold and Over Limit badges describe the Bill To.
rows.note: Credit Hold pill; Over Limit BT-N09

rows.prd_words: The customer's own Credit Hold does not block when someone else is billed.
When the customer pays for itself, Credit Hold reads and blocks exactly as today ("This customer is on Credit Hold!", "Cannot invoice this customer. Customer is on Credit Hold").
Without permission to change the Bill To, M2 shows with no button.
Once invoiced, the banner reads as today.
Later changes to the Bill To's name, address or terms never change an existing invoice.
A full-width band prints directly under the address row, reading "SERVICE FOR", then the customer's name in bold.
On a work order with an asset, the band adds "Unit [unit]" and "[year] [make] [model]", separated by " · ".
Missing unit, year, make or model parts drop out with their separator; a unit already starting with "Unit" is not prefixed again.
rows.note: missing unit; 'Unit' prefix rule not shown

rows.prd_words: On a part sale with a vehicle attached, the band adds the unit as in S8-R2 and S8-R3; without a vehicle it prints only "SERVICE FOR" and the name.
The band has a light grey fill and a thin grey border so it reads in black and white.
The band prints on the modern and legacy layouts, invoice and estimate, part sale invoice and batch invoice.
rows.note: no part sale invoice, no modern batch, batch page 1 only: BT-N11

rows.prd_words: The band leaves the address row free for a future Ship To block.
rows.note: address row keeps Bill To and Remit payment to only

rows.prd_words: When the customer pays for itself, no band prints and the document is unchanged.
Invoices created before this release never print the band.
The send window lists the Bill To's contacts.
It pre-ticks the Bill To's contact marked Billing, else its first contact A to Z by name.
Staff can tick other contacts and type addresses, as today.
"For Customer" attachments behave as today: sent only when staff tick the box, which starts unticked.
While the Bill To's contacts load, the window shows a loading state, never the customer's contacts.
When the customer pays for itself, the list and the pre-ticked contact are exactly today's.
The invoice's receivable posts to the Bill To's account, on its Invoices tab, AR Aging and statements.
A deposit is taken on the account of whoever is the Bill To when it is recorded.
A credit for returned parts on a part sale goes to the Bill To.
A payment settles only invoices owed by the paying customer; one payment can cover several of its invoices across customers.
The server refuses a payment applied to another customer's invoice with M3.
The Bill To's Invoices tab shows a "Service For" column naming the customer the work was for.
The column is blank on rows billed to this customer for its own work.
A credit issued from an invoice created after release reduces the revenue of that invoice's customer.
A payment can use only deposits and credits held by the paying customer; otherwise it is refused with M5.
The "Service For" column is hidden when no row on the tab, before any search, is billed for someone else.
rows.note: hidden on an empty tab; 'before any search' BT-N14

rows.prd_words: The customer's own Invoices tab does not list invoices billed to someone else, so they cannot be paid from its side.
Payments and credits applied before this release are not re-checked.
Reverse works exactly as today: the invoice is removed and the work order goes back to Complete.
After Reverse, the Bill To field unlocks and can be changed.
Invoicing again bills the current Bill To with its current terms and PO rules.
The re-issued invoice keeps the same invoice number.
With anything applied, Reverse is refused as today; staff reverse payments or deposits first.
A deposit taken under the wrong Bill To must be reversed and taken again under the new Bill To (M1 says so).
Deleting a customer that is another customer's saved default is refused, opening a "Delete Customer" window.
The window shows the refusal message and each dependent customer as a link to its page.
The window has "Cancel" and "Remove As Default Bill To" buttons.
"Remove As Default Bill To" asks to confirm, in a window titled "Remove as default Bill To" with "Remove" and "Cancel".
Confirming clears the saved default on every dependent customer; open work orders keep their Bill To.
The user then deletes the customer again.
A customer that is the Bill To on any work order or part sale cannot be deleted, with today's message "Company with a work order cannot be deleted."
Today's delete refusals come first; the "Delete Customer" window shows only when being another customer's default is the only reason.
Without 'Customers → Create & Edit' and 'View and Manage AP/AR Data', "Remove As Default Bill To" is hidden.
Each Bill To change adds a "Bill To changed" entry on the work order or part sale log.
The entry shows "Bill To" with the old and new customer, each as a link.
A Change Customer that moves the Bill To other than simply with the customer adds the same entry.
A plain Change Customer on a self-billed document adds only today's customer change entry.
Without 'Customers → View', the names show without links.
The tab lists every service work order on the asset at the current location, for every customer, in today's sort.
A "Customer" filter chip sits beside Status, defaulting to "All customers".
Its options are every customer on the asset's work orders, as customer or Bill To, A to Z.
The filter is multi-select; a work order matches when a picked customer is its customer or its Bill To.
With more than 8 options, the chip offers search ("Search customers").
A "Bill To" column shows when at least one row bills someone else; it is blank on self-billed rows.
The Customer filter resets when another asset is opened.
When the Status filter includes Imported, the Customer filter is disabled and cleared.
Internal and No Charge work orders have no Bill To; the field is hidden.
Converting to No Charge, or changing to an internal customer, resets the Bill To to the customer.
Converting back to billable starts from the customer's saved default, else the customer.
An internal customer is never offered or accepted as a Bill To.
The customer alone decides whether a work order is internal; the Bill To never does.
Until SV-11665 ships, every work order is billable and these rules have nothing to act on.
The Bill To's portal contacts see the invoice and can pay it.
The customer's portal contacts see the invoice read-only, with "Billed to [Bill To]" where Pay would be.
The "invoice created" email goes to the Bill To's portal contacts only.
Paying several invoices at once includes only invoices the viewer's customer owes.
The Bill To's contacts see only invoices that name their customer, not the customer's other jobs or assets.
A deposit link remembers the Bill To the work order had when staff created it.
If the work order's Bill To has changed since, paying the link is refused with G3 before any card is charged; no deposit is recorded.
When the customer pays for itself, the portal is unchanged.
The invoice is sent to QuickBooks with the Bill To as its customer.
A customer already linked to a QuickBooks customer always syncs to that one, whatever either is named.
A customer with no link is matched to the QuickBooks customer with exactly the same name, and linked to it.
If that QuickBooks customer is already linked to another ShopView customer, the invoice is not sent and appears on the Unexported report with Q1.
Reverse deletes the QuickBooks invoice, and the re-issued invoice is sent as new, as today.
If QuickBooks is not connected, nothing is sent and invoicing works as without the integration.
Invoices created before this release are not re-sent.
The invoice reaches AccountingHub with the Bill To as its customer.
What AccountingHub receives keeps its current format; no AccountingHub change is needed.
AccountingHub AR, aging and balances therefore group by the Bill To.
Reverse keeps the reversal record in AccountingHub and the re-issued invoice arrives as a new event, as today.
Payments, deposits and credits arrive under the Bill To's account.
When the customer pays for itself, AccountingHub receives what it receives today.
IBS uses the Bill To's IBS account: its remit-to, approval and batch.
The Bill To's IBS number is saved on the invoice when it is created, blank when the Bill To has none.
The remit-to, the "(IBS#: [number])" after the Bill To's name and the IBS batch read the saved number.
If the Bill To has no IBS account, the invoice does not go through IBS, even if the customer has one.
In the invoice CSV export, "Customer" is the Bill To and "Terms" is the term saved on the invoice.
The export's last column, "Service Customer", names the customer the work was for when someone else is billed.
The Public API adds the Bill To to work orders and invoices; existing customer fields keep naming the customer.
The Public API work order and invoice lists accept an optional Bill To filter; a malformed id returns an error.
The Public API changelog announces the addition.
Creating an invoice through the Public API for a Bill To on Credit Hold is refused.
"Service Customer" is blank when the invoice bills its own customer.
Invoices created before this release export exactly as before.
The Public API cannot set a Bill To or read a saved default.
A later change to the Bill To's IBS account never changes an existing invoice; invoices created before this release read the current account.

"This work order has a [$amount] deposit from [customer]. Reverse it, change the Bill To, then take the deposit again under the new Bill To." — Field tooltip; on click, error toast with "Open Deposits"
rows.trigger: Change the Bill To while one deposit is held
rows.note: word for word; toast adds Close (BT-D02); tooltip position BT-D08

rows.prd_words: "This work order has [$total] in deposits from [customer]. Reverse them, change the Bill To, then take the deposits again under the new Bill To." — Same as above
[customer] reads "[N] customers" — Same as above
rows.trigger: Deposits from more than one customer

rows.prd_words: "work order" reads "part sale" — Same as above
"Cannot invoice. The Bill To customer, [Bill To], is on Credit Hold" — Banner with "Change Bill To"; Create Invoice tooltip; error toast with "Change Bill To"
rows.trigger: Create Invoice when the Bill To is on Credit Hold
rows.note: banner word for word; tooltip and toast BT-N09; placement BT-D10

rows.prd_words: "This payment can only be applied to invoices billed to [customer]." — Standard error toast
rows.trigger: Payment applied to another customer's invoice

rows.prd_words: "This payment can only use deposits and credits held by [customer]." — Standard error toast
rows.trigger: Payment uses a deposit or credit held by another customer

rows.prd_words: "Invoiced. Reverse the invoice to change who's billed." — Field tooltip; on click, error toast with "Go To Invoice"
rows.trigger: Change the Bill To on an Invoiced document

rows.prd_words: "Counter Sale can't be the Bill To for another customer." — Standard error toast
rows.trigger: Counter Sale picked as a Bill To or default

rows.prd_words: "Counter Sale always bills itself." — Standard error toast
rows.trigger: A default saved on Counter Sale

rows.prd_words: "This customer is the default Bill To for [names, comma separated]. Remove it from [that customer / those customers] first." — "Delete Customer" window with links, "Cancel", "Remove As Default Bill To"
rows.trigger: Delete a customer that is someone's default

rows.prd_words: "Remove [customer] as the default Bill To for [N] [customer / customers]? Open work orders keep their Bill To." — Confirmation with "Remove", "Cancel"
"Company with a work order cannot be deleted." — Standard error toast (today's message)
rows.trigger: Delete a customer that is a Bill To on any work order

rows.prd_words: "New work orders and part sales for [customer] will be billed to this customer. Existing ones don't change." — Static line
"New work orders and part sales bill to this customer. Existing ones don't change." — Static line
"Customers billed to this customer by default" / "[customer] pays for" / "These customers bill new work orders and part sales to [customer] by default." — Tooltip; window with "Close"
"Billed to [Bill To]" — In place of Pay
rows.trigger: Customer's contact views an invoice billed to someone else

rows.prd_words: "QuickBooks customer [name] is already linked to another ShopView customer." — Unexported report reason; invoice not sent
rows.trigger: QuickBooks: same-name customer linked to another ShopView customer

rows.prd_words: "This work order is now billed to another customer. Contact the shop." — Portal payment error; no card is charged
rows.trigger: Customer portal: a deposit link is paid after the work order's Bill To changed
